s013.description:
Digital arrest scam explained: a "police officer" on a video call says you're under arrest — and the only way out is to move your money.
How the fake video-call arrest works, and the one rule that beats it.

One woman in India lost about ₹2.5 crore (~$260,000) in a single week. In 2024, Indians reported over 1.2 lakh digital-arrest cases and lost ₹1,918 crore (over $200 million). Police and agencies do not arrest anyone over a video call, and they never ask you to transfer money. On 29 Oct 2026 India's Supreme Court said banks that miss red flags should compensate victims. Dollar figures are approximate (₹95 ≈ $1).

Sources:
https://www.medianama.com/2026/10/223-sc-rbi-banks-compensate-digital-arrest-victims/
https://theprint.in/india/governance/after-465-spike-in-2024-mha-data-shows-digital-arrest-scams-are-on-a-decline-in-india/2857002/

s013.comment: Would you have hung up? 👇 Real police in India don't arrest anyone over a video call — and never ask you to move money (I4C advisory).

s014.description:
Is no-cost EMI really free? How 0% interest instalment plans hide the interest in the price.
No-cost EMI vs paying cash: where the hidden cost goes.

The bank still charges interest — the store usually covers it by dropping the discount cash buyers get. You can also pay tax on that hidden interest plus a processing fee. In the illustrative example in this video (a $300 phone, $255 for cash buyers), the instalment buyer pays about 21% more. In 2013 the Reserve Bank of India told banks that the very concept of zero percent interest is non-existent. Not financial advice.

Sources:
https://www.rbi.org.in/Scripts/NotificationUser.aspx?Id=8461
https://blog.mypaisaa.com/what-is-no-cost-emi/

s015.description:
Gold jewellery making charges explained: why a $1,000 gold necklace can sell back for around $800 even if the gold price doesn't move.
Dhanteras gold buying: jewellery vs coins and bars.

Making charges pay for design and labour — on necklaces at big jewellers they are often around 20% or more, and GST applies on top. When you sell or exchange, jewellers generally pay for the gold content only; making charges and the purchase tax are not added back. Coins and bars usually carry much lower charges. Dhanteras is on 6 Nov 2026. Not financial advice.

Sources:
https://gullak.money/blog/gold-making-charges/
